data.gender_notes: Euphemia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word eu (good) and pheme (speech). This name was given to honor those who spoke kind and gentle words, particularly those who used euphemisms. The name Euphemia carries the meaning “Good Speech” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Euphemia usually hope their child will grow to embody good speech and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies speaking words of kindness and encouragement.
data.etymology: Euphemia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Good Speech.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Euphemia total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: אופמיה
in_hebrew.meaning: מילה יפה, קול יפה, דיבור טוב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אופמיה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אופימיה' (Euphemia), שמשמעותה 'דיבור טוב' או 'מילה יפה'. השם משלב את המילים 'אופו' (eupho) שמשמעותו 'לדבר טוב' ו-'מיה' (hemia) שמשמעותו 'שם' או 'כינוי'. השם אופמיה משקף את הרעיון של דיבור טוב ומילה יפה, שיכולים להביא שמחה ואושר לאחרים. השם מופיע בתקופה היוונית והרומית והיה בשימוש נרחב בקרב הנוצרים הראשונים.

in_greek.name: Εὐφημία
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Εὐφημία προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑλληνικὴ λέξη 'εὐφημία' (euphemia), ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'καλή ομιλία' ἢ 'καλὸς λόγος'. Ἡ λέξη εὐφημία συνδυάζει τὰ 'εὐ-' (eu-) ποὺ σημαίνει 'καλός' καὶ '-φημία' (pheme) ποὺ σημαίνει 'ὄνομα' ἢ 'φήμη'. Ἡ Εὐφημία ἀπεικονίζει τὴν ἰδέα τῆς καλῆς καὶ εὐάρεστης ομιλίας, ἡ ὁποία μπόρεῖ νὰ φέρει χαρά καὶ εὐτυχία στοὺς ἄλλους. Τὸ ὄνομα Εὐφημία ἦταν συνηθέστερο στὴν ἄρχαια Ἑλλάδα καὶ κατὰ τὴν περίοδο τῆς Ρωμαϊκῆς Αὐτοκρατορίας.

in_latin.name: Euphemia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Euphemia is derived from the Greek word 'εὐφημία' (euphemia), which means 'good speech' or 'well-speaking'. The term euphemia combines 'εὐ-' (eu-), meaning 'well' or 'good', and '-φημία' (pheme), meaning 'speech' or 'fame'. Euphemia conveys the idea of speaking well and kindly, which can bring joy and happiness to others. The name was used in ancient Greece and Rome, and was popular among early Christians.

in_english.name: Euphemia
in_english.long_meaning: The name Euphemia originates from the Greek words 'εὐ' (eu), meaning 'well' or 'good', and 'φημία' (pheme), meaning 'speech' or 'fame'. Euphemia signifies good speech, well-speaking, or fair fame. The name has been used since ancient Greece and Rome and was popularized among early Christians. Euphemia symbolizes the power of kind and gentle speech, conveying a sense of warmth, compassion, and sincerity. The name is associated with positive qualities such as eloquence, diplomacy, and tactfulness.

Euphemisms, which are indirect expressions that may be more polite or less offensive, have played a significant role in social etiquette and diplomacy.

This notion aligns with the teachings of Jesus, who encouraged His followers to love their neighbors as themselves and to use words that build up rather than tear down.

historical_references.reference:
Euphemia of Chalcedon was a 5th-century Christian martyr. She was a young girl who was martyred during the Roman persecution of Christians. According to legend, she was offered to the pagan goddess Artemis in place of a sacred bull, but refused to comply, and was subsequently tortured and killed.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

Euphemia of Syria was a 4th-century Christian saint who is venerated in the Eastern Orthodox, Roman Catholic, and Anglican Churches. She is believed to have been a virgin and a healer, and was martyred during the persecution of Christians under the Roman Emperor Diocletian.
Source: Catholic Encyclopedia.
